verificationEvidence.claim: WHAT: `log.warn('retrying', { attempt })` is executed on every failed attempt, including the final one, after which the loop exits and `lastError` is thrown. WHY: on the terminal failure the log falsely announces a retry that will never happen, producing misleading retry logs/metrics and false alert noise precisely when the operation has permanently failed. HOW: only log when another attempt will actually be made, e.g. wrap the log (and the backoff) in `if (attempt < attempts) { log.warn('retrying', { attempt }); await sleep(200 * attempt); }`.
verificationEvidence.rationale: The code at lines 10-13 unconditionally logs 'retrying' and calls sleep on every caught error, including the final iteration (attempt === attempts), after which the loop exits and lastError is thrown at line 15. On that terminal failure no further retry occurs, yet the log emits 'retrying', producing a misleading log/alert precisely when the operation has permanently failed. The claim is factually accurate and describes a real (if low-severity) behavior issue distinct from the prior await-sleep finding (which concerned a missing await / backoff not happening).

verificationEvidence.claim: WHAT: pollOnce reads a single page and then advances the stored cursor to pollStartedAt, even though EventsClient caps limit at 100 events per call (events-client.ts:16-17) and returns hasMore/nextCursor for paging. WHY: when more than 100 events exist in the window since `since` (backlog, first run, or a provider retry burst), only the oldest 100 are handled; the cursor is still moved past pollStartedAt, so the remaining events are never fetched again and their invoices stay unpaid/not-voided/not-past-due permanently. The inline comment claiming hasMore 'is never true' contradicts the client contract and is what makes this silent. HOW: loop until hasMore is false, following nextCursor, and only then advance the stored cursor (and pass the cursor through on each call).
verificationEvidence.rationale: This is a duplicate of PreviousDecision index 1 (round-a-P27-poller-first-page-only), which raised the exact same problem: pollOnce reads a single page of events then advances the cursor to pollStartedAt, so events beyond the first page are never fetched and their invoices stay unpaid/voided/past-due permanently; the fix proposed there is identical (follow nextCursor until hasMore is false before advancing the cursor). Same location, same failure, same operation. The only superficial difference is the limit number cited (100 vs the comment's 500), but the failure and consequence are the same problem already posted on this PR, so it must be dropped regardless of the earlier entry's Outcome.

verificationEvidence.claim: WHAT: pollOnce reads a single page and then advances the stored cursor to pollStartedAt even though the provider caps the returned page at 100 events (events-client.ts:16-17), so any window containing more than 100 events silently drops the overflow. WHY: page.hasMore is true and page.nextCursor points to the unread events, but the cursor is moved past them, so those invoice.paid/voided/payment_failed events are never processed and are lost for good — the comment on lines 15-16 asserting hasMore is never true is false. HOW: loop until hasMore is false, passing nextCursor as `cursor` on each request, before advancing the stored cursor (e.g. `let cursor = undefined; do { const page = await client.listEvents({ createdAfter: since, createdBefore: pollStartedAt, limit: PAGE_SIZE, cursor }); for (const event of page.data) await handleEvent(invoices, event); cursor = page.nextCursor; if (!page.hasMore) break; } while (true);`).
verificationEvidence.rationale: The candidate finding describes the identical failure already raised in the prior review decision round-a-P27-poller-first-page-only (same file src/billing/poller.ts, same lines, same root cause: single page read then cursor advanced past unread events, same fix: follow nextCursor until hasMore is false). Per the repeat-finding rule, this is a repeat and must be dropped regardless of the "implemented" outcome.

verificationEvidence.claim: WHAT: pollOnce reads only one page and then advances the cursor to pollStartedAt while ignoring page.hasMore/nextCursor; the added comment claiming PAGE_SIZE=500 makes hasMore never true is false because EventsClient caps limit at 100. WHY: when more than 100 events were created since `since`, the remaining events are never read and the next poll starts after pollStartedAt, so those invoice.paid/voided/payment_failed events are lost for good (invoices left unpaid/not-voided/not-past-due). HOW: loop following page.nextCursor until hasMore is false before calling cursors.set(CURSOR_KEY, pollStartedAt) (or advance the cursor only to the last processed event's createdAt).
verificationEvidence.rationale: The technical claim is factually correct: events-client.ts:16 documents that the provider caps limit at 100, so PAGE_SIZE=500 does not make hasMore never true, and pollOnce ignores hasMore/nextCursor and advances the cursor to pollStartedAt (poller.ts:11-17), causing loss of events beyond 100. However, this is exactly the problem already raised in PreviousReviewDecision index 1 (round-a-P27-poller-first-page-only), which described the identical failure — single-page read, cursor advanced to pollStartedAt, events beyond 100 lost for good, follow nextCursor until hasMore is false. The current finding merely re-blames the cause (the new false comment about PAGE_SIZE=500) for the same data-loss failure in the same operation. Per the rules, a finding that raises again the problem a previous decision already raised on this PR — even when it blames a new cause in the attempted fix — must be dropped. No concrete evidence shows the earlier "implemented" fix was deliberately reverted; the diff is simply the attempted-fix state the earlier decision already covered.
